A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same circuit-discovery complexity study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial relocation of material.

before.justification: v1 reports complexity theorems, reductions and analytical constructions, including in Appendices A–M. It discusses experiments attributed to other work but reports no original empirical outcomes.

after.justification: v3 remains a theoretical study. Its retained proofs and added appendix discussions contain no original experimental, simulation, user-study or data-analysis results.

M1.justification: The MLP architecture, circuit-query procedures and quasi-minimality algorithms are retained. In particular, the binary-search procedures in Theorems 27 and 71 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or empirical tasks. The added discussion of continuous inputs and transformer applicability does not introduce evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons. Added citations and discussion of existing interpretability methods do not constitute new comparators.

E3.justification: Neither version provides an empirical evaluation protocol. Theoretical network parameters and proof constructions are not training or testing settings.

E4.justification: Neither version reports empirical ablations, robustness tests or case studies. Circuit ablation and robustness remain formal computational problems; the new supplementary discussion adds interpretation rather than experimental analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical tests. The retained probabilistic approximation schemes are theoretical definitions, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 4 changes the global Unbounded Minimal SC decision/search entry from NP-hard and membership in Sigma_2^p to an open-problem question mark. This changes a reported theoretical finding; there are no empirical scores to compare.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.6 explains how zero input weights and appropriate biases extend the local hardness constructions to integer and continuous inputs. Table 4 also withdraws the unbounded global minimal-SC classification. The numbered theorem statements and substantive proofs otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central complexity and quasi-minimality contributions remain. Section 5 removes the specific suggestion that the Conmy et al. (2023) procedure could reduce forward passes from n to log2(n), narrowing a practical algorithmic claim while retaining the underlying appendix algorithm.

C2.justification: Section 5 and new Appendices A.6 and N substantially expand interpretation and applicability. They introduce the redundancy-versus-identifiability tradeoff, distinguish exponential search spaces from proven intractability, and discuss worst-case versus average-case analysis, continuous inputs/outputs and additional routes to practical tractability.

D1.justification: No implementation, hardware, training-budget or code/data-access information is added or removed. Existing algorithm descriptions and construction parameters are retained; relocated parameter tables do not add reproducibility details.

R1.justification: Section 1.3 adds comparisons with neural-network learning complexity and minimum circuit-size research, and acknowledges the authors' earlier dissertation and conference work. Additional citations connect circuit queries to overlap and false negatives, while the central research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 substantially revises the explanatory structure: Section 3 consolidates complexity material, Section 5 becomes an organized set of future directions, and the appendix gains a contents page, preliminary remarks and supplementary discussion. The abstract and several explanatory passages are also edited.

P2.justification: Tables 1–3 and 5–11 move from the final pages to their relevant discussions. Table 4 is substantially condensed and removes the unresolved Count NC row. A new Figure 1 illustrates circuit relationships; the existing reduction figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 improves accessibility through contextual table placement, the circuit diagram and appendix navigation. Added discussion clarifies applicability and redundancy tradeoffs, while Table 4 explicitly marks a previously asserted classification as open. These are useful improvements in exposition and precision; the underlying theoretical contribution remains largely unchanged.
